title: Introduce strand-aware request bundler and SLA-sensitive ramp calibrator
author: Anya Petrov
description: Motivation: We observed recurring fatigue in p95/p99 during short-lived microbursts where naive batching either over-aggregates unrelated sequences or leaves hot strands undersampled. This PR adds two complementary pieces: 1) a strand-aware request bundler that groups concurrent requests by inferred request 'strand' (derived from session metadata and request fingerprinting) to keep logical locality and avoid mixing cold/warm hotpaths, and 2) an SLA-sensitive ramp calibrator that automatically shapes synthetic ramp traffic used by benchmarks to honor per-cohort latency SLOs while still exercising tail behavior. Design: The bundler runs as a lightweight pre-batcher stage in the bench runner pipeline. It computes a 64-bit strand key using a two-stage hash (session id + tokenized prompt signature) and maintains short-lived strand windows to enforce affinity for microbatch assembly. Bundles are limited by both token budget and strand diversity thresholds to prevent head-of-line blocking from long sequences. The calibrator observes running telemetry (p50/p95/p99 and queue depth) and adjusts derived ramp slopes and inter-arrival jitter to match target SLOs per cohort. It supports fixed-profile, closed-loop, and hybrid modes (default: hybrid). Implementation summary: - New module benchlab/bundler/strand_bundler.go (Go) and a small shim benchlab/bundler/bundler_test.go covering deterministic hashing and window eviction invariants. - New calibrator benchlab/ramp/calibrator.py (Python) used by the orchestration harness; it exposes a dry-run mode and a live mode that emits adjustment signals over an internal control topic. - Integration glue in benchlab/orchestrator/synth_runner.go that wires bundler output into the existing microburst generator. - Added a lightweight prometheus exporter benchlab/metrics/strand_metrics.prom with strand-level counters and a sampling histogram for bundle sizes. Testing: Unit tests cover hashing corner cases and bundler eviction. End-to-end benchmarking run against a 4-GPU mini-cluster (g4dn-style nodes) with seq-length mixes: 8/32/128. Results: Compared to baseline microburst runner, hybrid bundler+calibrator reduced p99 CPU latency amplification events by ~22% and lowered synthetic-run cost (measured tokens/sec-to-sla ratio) by ~13% on our steady-state profile. Docs and examples: Added README with configuration knobs and a short quickstart script to reproduce local runs. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test (local mini-cluster) - [x] Perf comparison (results attached below) - [x] Prometheus metrics wired - [x] Added Linear links and runbook notes Migration notes: No infra migration required. Default mode is off; opt-in via orchestrator config. Related: ENG-1289 (microburst stability epic), ENG-1334 (cohort-aware sampling).

review_comments: Kenta Mori: Nice work. Two quick asks: (1) can we expose the strand window TTL as a config knob (default 200ms) and document expected tradeoffs? (2) the bundler's deterministic hash seems to use the raw prompt; can we normalize whitespace to avoid churn?
Author (Anya Petrov): Reply: Added a config knob strand_window_ttl_ms and normalized prompt before hashing. See benchlab/config/synth_profiles.yaml and bundler_test for coverage.
Riley Thompson: Tests look good. Calibrator logic LGTM but please add a short note in the runbook about failure modes when telemetry is noisy.
Author: Added failure-mode notes in benchlab/README/strand_bundler.md and added an e2e flag --calibrator-noisy-check to gate live adjustments.
